Al Jazeera — 15 Nov 2026 (FULL-TEXT via WebFetch; extracted key paragraphs and quotes)

Estonia to close border crossings with Russia after attack on drone maker

Estonia will shut its border crossings with Russia following an attempted arson attack on drone manufacturer Threod Systems. Eight individuals were arrested in connection with the incident, which Estonian authorities attribute to Russia's GRU military intelligence.

Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna stated on X: "Russia must understand that hostile actions against Estonia come with consequences. Attempts to intimidate, destabilise, or undermine our security will not go unanswered."

He added that border closure aims to "reduce Russia's ability to conduct hostile activities in Estonia and strengthen our efforts to prevent sanctions circumvention." No timeline for reopening was specified.

Latvia's Interior Minister Janis Dombrava confirmed several "Latvian citizens and non-citizens" were among those arrested, noting that "since the collapse of the USSR, there have been people among us who are willing to commit serious crimes in Russia's interests."

Marko Mihkelson, chairman of Estonia's Parliament Foreign Affairs Committee, characterised this as part of Russia's broader "shadow war" against Europe, calling for allied nations to "respond with asymmetric measures of their own."

Estonia currently maintains three open border crossings with Russia: Narva, Luhamaa, and Koidula.

A Russian foreign ministry spokeswoman dismissed the measures as "aggressive and unrestrained Russophobia."
